input: Audit my monthly grocery spending habits

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this covers all food spending (dining out, takeaways, meal kits) or strictly supermarket/grocery-store purchases changes what data needs to be collected and what counts as in-scope.
A target budget or spending ceiling is the benchmark against which the audit is measured — without it, there is no clear standard for 'too much' or 'just right'.
The number of people the grocery spending covers (solo, couple, family) drastically affects what reasonable spending looks like and how to interpret the data.
The data source — bank statements, a budgeting app, paper receipts — determines the format of the audit and how much manual work is involved in gathering data.
Whether this is a solo self-review or involves a partner/housemate affects who contributes data and who needs to act on the findings.
The desired outcome — cutting costs, understanding category breakdowns, reducing waste, or just having a clear picture — determines what the audit should produce and how success is measured.
How the findings are presented (a simple list, a spreadsheet, a visual chart) affects how actionable the audit feels and how much effort goes into building it.

gold.taskTitle: Audit my monthly grocery spending habits
gold.taskDescription: Review and analyse the user's monthly grocery expenditure to identify patterns, inefficiencies, and opportunities to improve spending habits.

questions.title: What counts as grocery spending for this audit?
questions.description: Clarify whether the audit covers only supermarket and grocery-store purchases, or also includes takeaways, restaurant meals, meal-kit subscriptions, and similar food-related expenses.

questions.title: Do you have a monthly budget target in mind?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a specific spending limit or goal the user is trying to hit, which will serve as the benchmark for evaluating the audit findings.

questions.title: How many people does this grocery spending cover?
questions.description: Determine the household size so that spending totals can be contextualised and compared against realistic per-person benchmarks.

questions.title: Where is your spending data currently stored?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has bank statements, a budgeting app (e.g. YNAB, Mint), saved receipts, or no existing records — this shapes the entire data-gathering step.

questions.title: Are you doing this audit alone or with someone else?
questions.description: Determine whether a partner, housemate, or family member shares the grocery spending and needs to be involved in both the data collection and the resulting decisions.

questions.title: What is the main outcome you want from this audit?
questions.description: Clarify the primary goal — e.g. reducing total spend, identifying which categories overspend, spotting waste, or simply having a clear financial snapshot — so the audit is structured to deliver it.

questions.title: How do you want the findings presented to you?
questions.description: Establish the preferred output format — a written summary, a spreadsheet with category breakdowns, a visual chart, or an action-item checklist — so the audit is immediately usable.
